findings.title: Slots inside a date override skip the busy-time check, allowing double bookings
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable, the new code returns early: if a date override exists for the slot's day and the slot falls within the override range, `dateOverrideExist` is true and the function returns `true` (available) at line 133-135 before ever reaching the `busy.every(...)` conflict check at the bottom. Since checkIfIsAvailable is the only place a fixed host's busy times/bookings are consulted, any existing booking or calendar busy time that falls inside a date-override window is ignored, and the slot is shown as bookable. Consequence: fixed hosts (and round-robin hosts via the looseHostAvailability path, which spreads the same schedule object) can be double-booked on days that have a date override. The busy check must still run when the slot is inside an override.

findings.title: Working-hours check compares slot start against itself instead of slot end
findings.body: In the new workingHours validation inside checkIfIsAvailable, both `start` and `end` are computed from `slotStartTime`: `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();`. This was clearly meant to be `slotEndTime` (slot start + eventLength). As written, a slot that starts inside working hours but ends after the working-hours end (e.g. a 60-minute slot starting 30 minutes before the end of a fixed host's availability) is treated as within hours and kept. Consequence: bookings can be created that extend past the fixed host's availability boundary, which is exactly the class of bug this PR is trying to fix.

findings.title: Host with no working hours on the slot's weekday is treated as available
findings.body: The new workingHours check in checkIfIsAvailable only returns a match (and thus rejects the slot) when a workingHour exists whose `days` includes the slot's day AND the slot is outside its times. If the host has no working hour entry at all for that weekday (e.g. a fixed host who works Mon-Fri only, while the aggregated round-robin availability still produces Saturday slots from the other host's hours), `workingHours.find(...)` returns undefined, the check is skipped, and the slot passes as long as the host isn't busy. Consequence: fixed hosts remain bookable on days they don't work at all — the new enforcement only covers days where the host has partial hours. The check should reject the slot when no working hour covers that day.

findings.title: Multiple date overrides on the same day make all slots unavailable
findings.body: The `dateOverrides.find(...)` callback returns `true` (meaning 'block this slot') as soon as the slot is outside the time range of the first override matching the day, and `find` short-circuits without examining the remaining overrides. If a host has two override ranges on the same date (e.g. 09:00-11:00 and 14:00-16:00, which cal.com allows as separate availability rows for one date), a slot at 15:00 is outside the 09:00-11:00 range so the callback returns true and the slot is blocked; conversely any slot inside one range is outside the other, so every slot on that day ends up blocked. Consequence: days with more than one override range incorrectly show zero availability.

findings.title: Override day matching formats the override date in the server's local timezone but the slot in UTC
findings.body: The day comparison uses `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').format('YYYY MM DD')` — `dayjs(Date)` is in local mode, so `format` renders in the Node server's local timezone — and compares it to `slotStartTime.format('YYYY MM DD')` where `slotStartTime` is explicitly `.utc()`. On any server not running in UTC, the override start instant shifted by the organizer offset can format to a different calendar date than its UTC date, so date overrides silently fail to match (or match the wrong day). The code only works because production/test servers happen to run in UTC. Use `dayjs.utc(date.start)` (or `.tz(organizerTimeZone)`) consistently for this comparison.

findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with === is always false
findings.body: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes') === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, 'minutes')` compares two distinct dayjs object references and can never be true; the intended check for a full-day 'unavailable' override (start equals end) never fires. This is currently masked for 00:00-00:00 blocked days because the later `slotStartTime.isAfter(end)` check catches them, but a blocked-day override stored with any non-midnight equal start/end (or a slot spanning that point) will incorrectly be treated as available. Use `.isSame(...)` instead of `===`.

findings.title: Override timezone shift wraps across midnight and lands on the wrong day/hours
findings.body: The new conversion computes startTime/endTime as `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, 'minute').hour() * 60 + ...minute()`. When the organizer-to-invitee offset shift moves the override across midnight (e.g. organizer in UTC+5:30 with a 00:30-02:00 override, invitee in UTC: offset = -330 minutes, shifting to 18:30-20:00 of the previous day), `.hour()` silently wraps to the previous/next day's wall-clock hours while the `activeOverrides` filter on line 207 still applies the override to the invitee day matching the override's own date. Result: slots are generated at wrong times on the wrong invitee day (and in some cases startTime > endTime, producing no or inverted ranges) whenever a date override crosses midnight after timezone conversion.

findings.title: override.timeZone is optional in the type but used unconditionally
findings.body: packages/types/schedule.d.ts declares `timeZone?: string` as optional on TimeRange, but getSlots now calls `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` without a fallback. When a caller passes date overrides without a timeZone, dayjs falls back to the server's guessed local timezone, so `organizerUtcOffset` — and therefore the shifted startTime/endTime — is computed against the wrong zone and the override is applied at incorrect times. Either make timeZone required on the override type or default it (e.g. to organizerTimeZone) before computing the offset.

findings.title: No test covers the fixed-host round-robin scenario the PR claims to fix
findings.body: The PR description states its primary fix is that date overrides of fixed hosts are respected for round-robin events, and all of the new checkIfIsAvailable logic (date-override filtering per fixed host, working-hours bounds, organizerTimeZone plumbing) serves that path. The added test only extends the existing personal single-user event 'Check for Date overrides' test with a second invitee timezone; there is no scenario with a ROUND_ROBIN event type, hosts with isFixed, or a fixed host's date override. The bugs in that new code path (busy times skipped inside overrides, slot end never checked against working-hours end, hosts with no hours on a weekday treated as available) would not be caught by the current suite.
